summary: Our team created a health monitoring system for astronauts to use and log their data in. Ensuring they are all mentally and physically capable for the days ahead in their space missions. in cooperating variables like nutrition, exercise, sleep, mental wellbeing and environmental factors ensuring it is as close as it can be to a real life scenario
details:
ASTRA (Crew Health Intelligence) is a web-based astronaut health monitoring platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It allows users to track cardiovascular health, sleep, hydration, nutrition, emotional wellbeing, and environmental conditions, including radiation, oxygen levels, and atmospheric pressure.

Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Visual Studio Code, ASTRA features interactive dashboards, personalised astronaut profiles, nutritional analysis, and health trend visualisations.

Our team's creativity lies in combining multiple aspects of astronaut health into one accessible platform. We considered factors such as microgravity, isolation, nutritional needs, environmental hazards, and limited medical resources.

ASTRA aims to improve health awareness, support early identification of potential risks, and demonstrate how integrated monitoring technology could contribute to safer, healthier, and more sustainable long-duration space missions.
